title: Two-scale semigroup criterion for the normalized Green trace
question: Can the finite Mellin bridge be reorganized as a two-scale semigroup criterion that isolates a short-time UV power budget from a late-time IR gap budget, and thereby expose the exact uniform inputs needed for a Green-trace bound?

new_perspective.principle: Treat the positive heat trace H(t)=sum_k exp(-t lambda_k) as a Euclidean semigroup observable. On 0<t<=tau, a mixed R-412 profile gives H(t)<=A_tau t^(-alpha_UV) after replacing the finite IR head by its mode count. On t>=tau, the first positive eigenvalue gamma gives H(t)<=H(tau) exp(-gamma(t-tau)).
route: Enumerate every R-412 exponent pair and interior split on every actual conditional likelihood row.
Build the pure short-time coefficient A_tau = r tau^alpha_UV + C_UV alpha_UV Gamma(alpha_UV), where the first term covers the finite IR head and the second covers the continuous UV tail.
Check the pointwise short-time power envelope, its integrable budget A_tau tau^(1-alpha_UV)/(1-alpha_UV), and the exact finite Mellin decomposition.
Use gamma=min(lambda_k) and H(tau) to test the late semigroup envelope and the integrated bound H(tau)/gamma.
Retain the row-wise best profile only as a finite diagnostic; promotion requires a fixed split, a uniform UV coefficient, a uniform positive gap, and a common Hamiltonian core.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: The short/late split is the finite analogue of separating ultraviolet proper-time renormalization from infrared spectral decay in a Euclidean QFT two-point function. It becomes physically useful only after regulator and volume uniformity, R-399 shell transfer, R-406 Schur control, and OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction are proved.

finite_theorem.short_time_envelope: For 0<t<=tau and 0<alpha_UV<1, H(t)<=A_tau t^(-alpha_UV), with A_tau=r tau^alpha_UV+C_UV alpha_UV Gamma(alpha_UV).
finite_theorem.late_time_envelope: For t>=tau and gamma=min_k lambda_k>0, H(t)<=H(tau) exp(-gamma(t-tau)).
finite_theorem.late_time_budget: integral_tau^infinity H(t)dt = sum_k exp(-tau lambda_k)/lambda_k <= H(tau)/gamma.
finite_theorem.scope: Every implication is finite-dimensional and rowwise; the quantities A_tau, gamma and H(tau) are not asserted to be uniform in a regulator, volume, source, phase or exhaustion.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar positivity of the semigroup factor and UV power budget; ordered spectra, Gibbs rows, graph construction, uniform gaps, common domains and QFT reconstruction remain executable/open analysis.

promotion_criteria: Prove a fixed or analytically controlled split time and a source/cutoff/volume/phase/exhaustion-uniform UV coefficient on one Hamiltonian common core.
Prove a positive source/cutoff/volume/phase/exhaustion-uniform intrinsic gap and bound H(tau) on the same core.
Transfer both budgets to the R-399 conditional shell and combine them with the R-406 Schur residual before any common-alpha or GNS promotion.
stop_conditions: If alpha_UV reaches 1 or above, the short-time power integral diverges and the criterion cannot be used.
If the first positive eigenvalue collapses under a validated cutoff or volume stress, retain only the UV half and do not claim an IR semigroup budget.
If the late factor uses max(lambda_k), a wrong sign, or omits H(tau), retain the failed inequality and do not promote it.
Finite two-scale checks are not a common-core, GNS, physical-gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite two-scale semigroup bridge only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform UV coefficient or IR gap, common core, common split rule, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The criterion isolates the exact UV coefficient, split-time heat trace and IR gap that a future uniform proof must control; the finite rowwise pass supplies no regulator-independent premise.
